Check a comparison of staged and live rows against rules

Source: R/run_compare.R
check_staged_against_live.Rd

check_staged_against_live() checks each key of a comparison from compare_staged_to_live() against the rules in rules. It stops with an error that names every failing key, and otherwise returns the comparison.

Usage

check_staged_against_live(
  comparison,
  rules = c("partitions_agree", "no_missing", "no_decrease")
)

Arguments

comparison

A data.table from compare_staged_to_live(). Every column except partition, staged and live is a key column.

rules

A character vector with one or more of "partitions_agree", "no_missing" and "no_decrease". An unknown name is an error.

Value

comparison, invisibly, when every key passes. Otherwise the function stops with an error of class cs9_staged_check_error. Its message names each failing key and its problem. Its element failures is a data.table with the key columns and problem, with one row per failing key.

Details

A key is live when a live row of any partition holds it. These are the rules:

  • partitions_agree: the partitions that hold the key have one value in the live rows, and one value in the staged rows. "One value" means that unique() of the values has length 1.

  • no_missing: a live key has a staged value.

  • no_decrease: no staged value of a live key is below a live value of it. A staged value equal to the live value passes.

no_missing and no_decrease pass a key that is not live. partitions_agree checks every key, also a key that is not live.

A key fails at most once, with the first problem in this order:

  1. the live partitions disagree on the stored total (<values>)

  2. the partitions disagree on the staged total (<values>)

  3. staged none, stored <values>

  4. staged <values>, stored <values>

<values> are the distinct values, sorted, without scientific notation, and separated by ", ". These texts and this order are those of consultations_check() in norsyss.cs9.

See also

compare_staged_to_live()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# In the action of a task that has the table `results` in its tables.
comparison <- compare_staged_to_live(tables$results, "isoyearweek", "n")
check_staged_against_live(comparison, rules = "no_decrease")
} # }
